extension.description: A Kodi metadata scraper for TV shows, backed by your self-hosted Chronicle server. Unlike a normal scraper, it never talks to TheTVDB or any other upstream source directly -- it only ever asks Chronicle, which resolves-and-creates the item through whichever metadata providers you've already configured there, so Kodi always ends up seeing exactly what Chronicle itself would show for that title -- seasons and episodes, multi-source ratings, and all. Movies are a separate sibling addon, script.chronicle.scraper.movie -- install both if you track both. They have to be separate addons: Kodi resolves which script to run for a scrape by addon id alone, not by which extension point (movies vs tvshows) triggered the call, so one addon declaring both would silently run the wrong script for TV every time. No Connect/Settings UI of its own -- copy the same Chronicle URL and API key from Chronicle Scraper (Movies)'s settings into this addon's settings. "Rebuild local NFOs from Chronicle" and the corner status indicator live in the Movies addon and cover both movies and TV shows together; this addon doesn't duplicate them.
extension.news: v1.0.1 - Three fixes, all found in code review: (1) lib/legacy_nfo.py's stash directory was still under special://profile/addon_data/{addon_id}/ in this addon's copy, scoped to this addon's own id -- meaning a TV show's stashed legacy-NFO data (harvested by this addon's delete step) could never be found by the re-scrape that consumes it, since that re-scrape also runs from this same addon's process but the path itself was never actually reachable in the intended cross-addon case. Now stashes under special://temp/chronicle_scraper/, matching rebuild_state.py and activity_tracker.py. (2) settings.xml had an invalid XML comment (a literal "--" inside the comment body, which XML never allows outside the opening/closing delimiters) -- replaced with an em dash. (3) strings.po's #32092 help text had unescaped literal quote marks inside its msgid, breaking that string's parsing -- now escaped to match the convention used everywhere else in this file. v1.0.0 - Split out of script.chronicle.scraper (now script.chronicle.scraper.movie) as its own addon, so Kodi can actually invoke the TV scraper -- see that addon's v3.0.0 changelog entry for the full root-cause explanation. Same code as tvshow_scraper.py always had (the v2.13.2 endOfDirectory fix and the v2.13.3 rebuild-pass-only NFO gating), just finally reachable.
